title: Anna Lewis v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
disposition_detail: The SJC held the BCO 40-5 filing out of order because Chapter 40 matters reached it only upon General Assembly referral.
first_summary: After her session erased her from the roll, Anna Lewis filed a BCO 40-5 report directly with the SJC, alleging the Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley failed to redress the session's alleged failure to give BCO 38-4 notice. The SJC held the filing out of order: under RAO 16-10.c and OMSJC Chapter 15, BCO Chapter 40 matters come to it only by General Assembly referral. It did not decide the merits, but noted that without proper notice Lewis remains a member unless she joined another church. Dissents disputed that limitation and cited past direct reviews.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The case page records the SJC decision and 17 concurring, six dissenting, and one disqualified vote.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lewis challenged Presbytery's failure to redress her Session's erasure of her name without alleged BCO 38-4 notice.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The decision itself calls this a filing with the SJC and found it out of order because Chapter 40 matters reached the SJC only by General Assembly referral.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The merits were not decided; the majority conditionally observed that absent notice Lewis remained a member unless she joined another church.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Not applicable; prior direct reviews appear in the dissents and are attributed accordingly.

source_limits: Complete adopted decision and separate opinions are present; the filing route appears in procedural background rather than an adopted factual finding.
